edition.alertText: Oil crashes to 3-month low — Brent falls ~3.8% to ~$88.95 as IEA declares first supply surplus since war began; Q4 glut projected; Kpler: Hormuz crude flows drop to ~9.5M b/d (10 days to Nov 19), down from 12.2M in October — steepest intra-month decline since war began; IRGC claims 3 more tankers hit mines in Hormuz on Monday — claims ships were under US escort; CENTCOM has not confirmed; Iran FM spokesman Baqaei vows to use 'every means' to counter US blockade — cites Article 51, calls blockade 'act of crime'; Trump (Sunday): Iranian ships breaking blockade would go 'to the bottom of the sea — just like the rest of their navy'; Vance and Rubio meet Qatari PM at White House and State Dept — biannual US-Qatar Strategic Dialogue; Iran talks stalled per AP; Houthis claim attack on Saudi Rabigh oil refinery on Red Sea coast; Saudi airstrike hits fuel station in Sanaa — 6 wounded (Houthi Health Ministry); Houthi attack on Hodeida kills 4, wounds 18; Iran imposes power cuts as domestic energy crisis deepens ahead of winter; gold rebounds 3.4% to ~$3,635 after crash to $3,532; S&P 500 rallies 4.8% led by Nvidia reinstating Jensen Huang as CEO (+31%); WTI falls to ~$80 — 3-month low; UKMTO weekly: 263 ships transited Hormuz Nov 12-18, down 15% WoW; oil tankers from 52 to 37 (-29%); Orbital Risk Intelligence: 15 attacks in week to Nov 20 — up 50% WoW, highest since mid-October; IEA's Birol: confidence in Hormuz shipping 'shattered'; Eisenkot says no immediate Iran threat requiring Israeli military action; OPEC+ meets Nov 29 on 2027 output — IEA surplus projection complicates expansion plans

situation: Oil prices crashed to three-month lows on Monday as a convergence of supply-side developments overwhelmed geopolitical risk premiums. The IEA's November Oil Market Report confirmed that global oil supply has exceeded demand for the first time since the Iran war began in February, projecting a surplus through the fourth quarter — a dramatic reversal from the acute shortage that drove Brent above $116 in late October. Brent fell approximately 3.8% to around $88.95/bbl, its third consecutive weekly decline, while WTI dropped to approximately $79.96/bbl. Kpler tracking data showed Hormuz crude flows averaging approximately 9.5 million b/d over the ten days to November 19, down sharply from 12.2 million b/d in October — the steepest intra-month decline since the war began. Goldman Sachs noted that the dated Brent physical premium over futures had collapsed from roughly $31/bbl in early October to approximately $1, signaling that the market's panic over supply has largely dissipated despite ongoing disruptions. Libya's Sharara pipeline restart further eased supply concerns. Despite the oil rout, equities surged: the S&P 500 rallied 4.8%, led by Nvidia which soared 31% after reinstating Jensen Huang as CEO. Gold rebounded 3.4% to approximately $3,635/oz, recovering from last week's crash to $3,532 as bargain hunters stepped in, though gold remains well below its October highs. The DXY dollar index rose 0.5% to its strongest level since March 2025.

The diplomatic landscape showed simultaneous escalation and engagement. Vice President JD Vance and Secretary of State Marco Rubio held separate meetings with Qatar's Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman bin Jassim Al Thani on Monday — Vance at the White House, Rubio at the State Department — as part of the biannual US-Qatar Strategic Dialogue. The Associated Press described Iran negotiations as 'stalled,' reporting that Trump had told Vance the administration did not need a deal with Iran and instructed him to focus on domestic priorities following the Republican midterm losses. At a Friday White House press conference, Trump said Tehran wants an agreement but not one 'acceptable' to him. On Sunday, responding to reports of Iranian tankers preparing to run the blockade, Trump warned that Iranian ships would go 'to the bottom of the sea — just like the rest of their navy.' Iran's foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei responded Monday by vowing to use 'every means' to counter the US blockade, calling it 'military aggression' and an 'act of crime' under the UN Charter. IRGC aerospace commander Majid Mousavi declared 'the field is ours and we determine the battlefield,' while deputy commander-in-chief Maj. Gen. Mostafa Izadi warned that any threat would draw a response 'without geographical limitations.' Israeli PM-designate Eisenkot said he sees no immediate Iranian threat requiring Israeli military action, a markedly different tone from Netanyahu's push for a campaign.

On the maritime front, the IRGC claimed on Monday that three more oil tankers suffered 'severe explosions and fires' after striking naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz, asserting the vessels were under US escort — CENTCOM had not confirmed the incidents. The IRGC warned that 'military cover and escort by the US military will not serve as a substitute for complying with maritime regulations.' This brought total war attacks past 286 by multiple tracking sources. Orbital Risk Intelligence reported 15 attacks and piracy incidents in the week to November 20, up 50% week-on-week and the highest weekly total since mid-October, with four tankers hit within 13 nautical miles of Khasab over three days. UKMTO's weekly overview showed 115 outbound and 148 inbound transits in the week to November 18, down from 139 and 169 the prior week, with transit volumes approximately 65% below pre-conflict levels. Iran has now designated 240 vessels on its Non-Compliance List (Vortexa), including 56% of Gulf shuttle tankers. In Yemen, Houthis claimed an attack on Saudi Arabia's Rabigh oil refinery on the Red Sea coast, while a Saudi airstrike reportedly hit a fuel station in Sanaa wounding six workers and a Monday strike on Hodeida killed four and wounded eighteen. The UN reported more than 1,600 dead and 300,000+ displaced in Yemen since July. Iran imposed domestic power cuts as it braces for a winter natural gas crisis, with the energy ministry warning of shortages amid wartime damage to infrastructure.

supplyChain.name: Sulfur
supplyChain.text: Global exports down 39% YoY to 6.1M tonnes in Q2 (S&P). Sulfur prices eased from June-July peaks of $1,100-1,300/tonne to $740-890/tonne by mid-October (Kpler), but remain above pre-war avg of ~$500/tonne (CRU). ADNOC sees sulfur output doubling from 7M to 14-20M tonnes by 2030-2035 — CEO Al Jaberi calls sulfur 'the future gold' (Nov 18). ADNOC's Oct official selling price cut $70 to $890/tonne. Morocco's OCP needs 3.7M tonnes/yr from the region. Nearly half of seaborne sulfur passed through Hormuz pre-war. Phosphate prices up 25-30%; DAP at $803/mt in October, ~30% above January (IFDC). Trade routes shifting as Morocco and China seek alternative sources (ChemAnalyst). China phosphate exports near zero in 2026, down from ~5.3M mt in 2025 (IFDC).

supplyChain.name: Sulfuric Acid
supplyChain.text: China banned exports Apr-Aug (700kt/yr quota replaced). SX-EW copper producers (15% of global cathode) fully exposed. Huayou cut Indonesian nickel HPAL output 50%.

supplyChain.name: Fertilizer
supplyChain.text: Fertilizer shipments through Hormuz at zero for seventh consecutive month — September through late November all zero (World Visualized/Syz Group/Fertilizer Daily). UN official Jorge Moreira da Silva at COP31 (Nov 14) warned 45 million people could face severe food insecurity — urged US and Iran to immediately allow ~5 fertilizer vessels/day through Hormuz within 7-10 days. Fertilizer prices up ~30% since blockades began (UN). WHO: Yemen death toll since August escalation reaches 2,260, with 10,519 wounded; more than 1,600 dead and 300,000+ displaced since July (UN); UNICEF: 330,000+ displaced including 174,000 children. Sudan food prices doubled in 6 months; Nepal farmers cannot afford fertiliser. Countries facing significant impact: Mozambique, Kenya, Sudan, Somalia, Nepal, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka. Urea exports from Hormuz-dependent economies fell 83% YoY in April (ITC). ~850kt urea stranded. 4 of 5 Bangladesh urea plants shut since March due to LNG shortages. Pakistan faces 200,000-ton fertiliser shortfall (Express Tribune). FAO Food Price Index at 136 (highest since Nov 2022). DAP at $803/mt in October, urea near January levels after April spike (IFDC Bulletin #37). Egypt gas supply cuts to fertilizer producers rose from 20% to 33% on Nov 8 — AGF Nitrogen running at 80-85% capacity (IFDC). Russia export quotas Dec 2026–May 2027 at ~18.8M mt, down from ~20M mt. IFPRI: no bypass route for ammonia or sulfur unlike crude. UN fertilizer corridor stalled pending US-Iran agreement. Middle East fertiliser exports declined by 70% as Iran war disrupts supplies (The National).

supplyChain.name: LNG
supplyChain.text: QatarEnergy extends LNG force majeure through end of December 2026 — 8th consecutive extension since April. Poland's Orlen becomes first buyer to terminate QatarEnergy LNG contract (1M tonnes/yr, oil-linked, through 2034) citing ongoing force majeure (S&P Global Platts, Nov 11). DES NW Europe LNG benchmark at $27.59/MMBtu on Nov 11, up 175% YoY. Qatar LNG loadings pick up to roughly half of pre-war levels (Bloomberg, Nov 10). 31 laden LNG tankers exited Hormuz in October — highest since war began (S&P Global). Global LNG supply gap estimated at ~600 bcf. Dutch TTF gas eased to ~€89.59/MWh (~$100.85); EU gas storage at 74.33% full vs 86% five-year average — lowest in over a decade entering winter (IEA). Natural gas futures fell 8.2% to $3.13/MMBtu (Nov 23). IRGC claims gas carrier exploded after mine strike in eastern Hormuz (Nov 13). Pakistan to pay >$1B for winter LNG spot cargoes at ~2x Qatari contract price. Lufthansa says 2026 fuel costs €2B higher amid Iran war. EIA projects US heating oil households to pay $2,977 this winter — up 70.2% from last year. IMF projects 2026 GDP contractions: Kuwait and Iraq ~16%, Qatar ~15%. LNG flows at 40-45% of prewar levels. Iran braces for winter natural gas shortages — imposes power cuts as energy crisis deepens (Nov 23).

supplyChain.name: Petrochemicals
supplyChain.text: MEG ethylene/polyethylene exports disrupted. Gulf petrochem complex cut to ~60% capacity. Methanol down 80% (ITC). Dow, LyondellBasell margins widening on supply constraint. ExxonMobil Q3 profit more than doubled to $15.4B on energy surge. Aramco Q3 profit surges 34.6% to $36.3B. Allianz Trade estimates >$200B in physical damage across GCC — 80+ energy facilities struck, a third severely damaged; cumulative economic losses projected at $790B through 2030. Arabian Gulf crude shipments fell 27.6% YoY to 531.3M tonnes in Jan-Oct 2026 — Gulf share of global seaborne crude fell from 39.8% to 30.6% (Banchero Costa/LSEG).
